thread.title: Messi Leads Argentina to World Cup Final with Dramatic Comeback Against England
thread.title_full: Messi Leads Argentina to World Cup Final with Dramatic Comeback Against England

author: Liam O'Connor Sports Editor
title: Messi Leads Argentina to World Cup Final with Dramatic Comeback Against England
text:
Argentina advanced to the 2026 FIFA World Cup final after a 2-1 comeback win over England in Atlanta, with Lionel Messi orchestrating two late assists to secure the victory. The win sends Argentina to a final against Spain on Sunday.
Late Drama and Messi’s Masterclass
Lionel Messi’s brilliance once again proved decisive as Argentina overturned a 1-0 deficit against England in the 2026 World Cup semifinal, scoring twice in the final 10 minutes to book a place in the final against Spain. The match, played at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, saw Argentina’s relentless pressure pay off as they won without holding the lead after 90 minutes of play in all four of their knockout rounds this tournament.
Messi provided both assists, showcasing his ability to control the game’s tempo and exploit space.
Fan Reactions: A Nation’s Passion
The victory sparked euphoria among Argentine fans, many of whom traveled across the globe to witness the team’s run. Sonia, an Argentina supporter, captured the national spirit, stating, “Argentinians, we feel football — soccer — in our blood. It’s in our veins,” according to CBS News. Fans like Gordon Maner, who traveled from South Carolina to see Messi, expressed excitement to see the Argentine captain return to another World Cup final.
Even non-Argentine fans were moved by the team’s resilience. Kamsi Okpala, who described herself as “not even from Argentina,” admitted, When he came back in 2022 and he won it, I literally cried. The emotional connection to Messi and the team’s fighting spirit transcended borders, as seen in the chants and banners that filled the stadium.
Tactical Missteps and the Road to the Final
England’s collapse, however, was as much a product of tactical missteps as it was of Argentina’s dominance. The Athletic detailed how England manager Thomas Tuchel’s decision to adopt a “back five” formation in the second half left his team vulnerable. This strategy, reminiscent of the “Azteca Plan” used against Mexico, allowed Messi to operate freely in the midfield, creating chances that England’s defense could not contain.
Tuchel’s choices drew sharp criticism, with The Athletic noting that England’s failure to utilize pace after taking the lead left them “deep underwater” by the final minutes. John Pyatt, an England fan who traveled from his home country to support the team, acknowledged the setback but praised England’s efforts: They’ve worked really hard. They fought hard the whole tournament.
Argentina’s Unyielding Legacy
Argentina’s ability to win in the final minutes has become a defining trait of this World Cup campaign. Yahoo Sports described the team as “the monster lurking under your bed,” emphasizing their knack for turning games around when opponents believe they have the upper hand. This pattern—coming from behind in every knockout round—has cemented their reputation.
Lautaro Martínez, who scored the winning goal, reflected on the team’s mentality, stating, “We had come off three tough matches where things got complicated, yet the team always managed to dig deep.” His words underscore a collective belief that Argentina is “a team that never settles and always wants more.”
What Comes Next: Spain Awaits
Argentina’s final against Spain on Sunday at MetLife Stadium promises to be a showdown of two titans of the sport. Spain, known for their technical prowess and tactical discipline, will face a team that has proven its ability to thrive under pressure. The match will test whether Argentina’s late-game magic can carry them to victory, or if Spain’s structured approach can finally halt their rise.
For now, Argentina’s fans can revel in a victory that has only deepened their bond with the team. As one supporter put it, “They find a way to win”—a mantra that has guided them through this tournament and now into the final. The world will be watching to see if they can make history once again.
